title: Writing the Answer as a Mixed Number

steps.body: An improper answer like 12/8 can be renamed as a mixed number: group the pieces into wholes and keep the leftovers as a fraction. The figure shows the same conversion direction with another value, 11/8 = 1 3/8; regroup 12/8 into complete groups of eight.
steps.narration: An improper answer like 12/8 can be renamed as a mixed number: group the pieces into wholes and keep the leftovers as a fraction. The figure shows the same conversion direction with another value, 11/8 = 1 3/8; regroup 12/8 into complete groups of eight.

widget.prompt: Build 10/4 and find how many wholes it holds.
widget.successFeedback: 10/4 — ten fourths, which groups into two wholes with two fourths left over.
widget.lowFeedback: Your bar represents less than the target value. Increase it until the values match.
widget.highFeedback: Your bar represents more than the target value. Decrease it until the values match.

commonFractions.feedback: 4/4 is exactly one whole; ten fourths holds more than two of them.
12/4 is three whole cups — one group too many; ten fourths stops short of that.

predict.reveal: Eight eighths make one whole, and twelve eighths contains exactly one such group plus four spare.

cml.actionGoal: Collect equal groups of a fraction and watch only the COUNT of pieces change for g4x mixed answer.
invariants: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number collects groups of identical pieces: the denominator names the piece size and holds still, while the numerator counts every piece gathered, which is what keeps g4x mixed answer a counting problem.
misconceptions: Scaling the denominator along with the numerator, adding the whole number to the numerator, or assuming a product cannot pass one whole.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the denominator DID change when you collected groups, what would happen to the size of each piece?

widget.prompt: Convert 10/3 to a mixed number. What is the WHOLE NUMBER part?

commonErrors.feedback: 10 counts the PIECES. Every 3 of them rebuild one whole, so ask how many groups of 3 fit.
That counted the leftover 1 thirds as another whole, but 1 is short of 3.

steps.body: Every 8 eighths rebuild one whole, so 12/8 is one whole with 4 eighths left over — 1 4/8, and the value has not moved.

widget.prompt: Regroup the pieces into wholes: convert 14/5 to a mixed number. What is the WHOLE NUMBER part?

commonErrors.feedback: Fourteen counts fifth-sized pieces; group them into sets of five.
Three complete wholes need fifteen fifths, but only fourteen are available.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Count how many complete groups of five fit into fourteen pieces.
widget.successFeedback: Correct — 14/5 = 2 4/5, so the whole-number part is 2.
